questions.stem: This fundoscopic photograph shows cotton-wool spots, arteriovenous nicking, and flame-shaped retinal hemorrhages around the optic disc. These retinal findings are the classic end-organ manifestation of which systemic condition?

explanation.summary: Arteriovenous nicking, cotton-wool spots (retinal ischemia), and flame hemorrhages reflect chronic hypertensive damage to the retinal arterioles, making the retina a window onto systemic hypertensive vascular injury.
explanation.whyCorrect: Arteriovenous nicking, cotton-wool spots (retinal ischemia), and flame hemorrhages reflect chronic hypertensive damage to the retinal arterioles, making the retina a window onto systemic hypertensive vascular injury.

questions.stem: These renal biopsy panels from a hypertensive patient show (A) glomeruli and an arteriole with homogeneous pink wall thickening and luminal narrowing, and (B) an arteriole with concentric 'onion-skin' laminated wall thickening. What vascular process do these images depict?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fibromuscular dysplasia of the renal artery

explanation.summary: Chronic hypertension produces hyaline arteriolosclerosis (homogeneous protein deposition in the wall) and, with more severe/malignant hypertension, hyperplastic 'onion-skin' arteriolosclerosis, both narrowing the lumen and driving nephrosclerosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chronic hypertension produces hyaline arteriolosclerosis (homogeneous protein deposition in the wall) and, with more severe/malignant hypertension, hyperplastic 'onion-skin' arteriolosclerosis, both narrowing the lumen and driving nephrosclerosis.
